text:
Anya: Heads up — we need a rate-limit redesign to make API key/org rate limits react to GPU pool saturation. Current static qps per-key causes queue explosion during pool hot-spots.

Mike: +1. What's the high-level idea?

Sophia: Per-org 'credit' buckets that refill at a rate proportional to the healthy headroom of the pools actually servicing that org. Credits consumed per request = cost estimate (model, seq_len). That lets us scale aggregate throughput down when pools are tight.

Dave: Who computes the refill? Central controller or edge proxies? Distributed systems detail will blow up if we centralize.

Anya: Central admission publishes per-pool headroom & per-org weight. Edge proxies pull a tiny allocation every 5s and enforce locally. Central stays SOT for weights/refill hints.

Lucy: We should avoid oscillation — use smoothing (EMA over 30–60s) and a min_refill floor. Also cap burst size so a single spike doesn't drain the system.

infra-bot: pool/eu-west/gpu-pool-3 util=92% free_slots=4 baseline_refill_factor=0.25

Anya: Example control config (pseudo):
```json
{
  "refill_window_s": 5,
  "min_refill": 0.1,
  "smoothing_tau_s": 45,
  "burst_cap": 10.0,
  "pool_weights": {"eu-west": 0.5, "us-east": 0.4, "ap-south": 0.1},
  "per_request_cost": {"gpt-xl": 1.0, "gpt-medium": 0.3, "rerank": 0.05}
}
```

Mike: How do we keep it fair? We can't let big orgs grab all elastic headroom.

Sophia: Give every org a baseline guaranteed credit (based on commit tier) and then split remaining headroom proportionally by configured weight. Also enforce a max share per-org in a window.

Dave: Enforcement model: proxies do fast path checks with local credit cache. If local cache misses, they request a refill token batch from central. This reduces RTT on steady state. Must plan for partitioned central controller — proxies should degrade to conservative local rate if disconnected.

Lucy: Rejection semantics: when credits exhausted we can 1) 429 immediate, 2) enqueue with a max_wait (e.g., 30s) and admit if credits return, or 3) auto-downgrade to cheaper model variant and charge less credit. Prefer (2) + (3) as progressive fallback. Also add Retry-After/backoff_hint headers.

Anya: Telemetry we need: credit_refill(rate, source_pool), credit_spent(org,key,request_cost), credit_reject(org,key,reason), queue_latency_ms. Add a small payload in response header with current_credit_estimate.

Mike: I'll build a simulator that replays historical traces and injects pool failures to validate stability. We'll tune smoothing_tau, min_refill, and burst_cap from sim.

Sophia: I'll prototype the smoothing and fairness allocator (weighted share + cap).

Dave: I'll add local proxy token cache + fallback to central with exponential backoff. Also design the disconnect policy.

Lucy: I'll own metrics schema + dashboards and the backoff_hint header spec.

Anya: Rollout plan: 1) offline sim and parameter sweep, 2) internal canary (5% traffic, single region), 3) regional ramp (50% eu-west), 4) full ramp. Each stage gated by queue latency, reject rate, and tail p99 token refill delta.

Mike: Timeline idea: sim ready in 5 business days -> canary next week if numbers look good.

Sophia: Action items recap: sim (Mike) due Mon; proxy prototype (Dave) due Wed; metrics schema + dashboard (Lucy) due Tue. I'll follow up with the fairness algo PR. :checkered_flag:

Anya: Thanks — this should reduce catastrophic queue growth and give us a tunable way to tie rate limits to real capacity rather than static QPS.

Lucy: Also let's add an emergency override to convert all orgs to conservative mode (min_refill) when any pool crosses 98% util.

Dave: noted, will add circuit-breaker flag and safety TTL.
